# zengate [![CI](https://github.com/developingchet/zengate/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/developingchet/zengate/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/zengate)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/zengate) [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/zengate)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/zengate) [![Docker Hub](https://img.shields.io/docker/v/developingchet/zengate?label=docker&sort=semver)](https://hub.docker.com/r/developingchet/zengate) [![Docker Pulls](https://img.shields.io/docker/pulls/developingchet/zengate)](https://hub.docker.com/r/developingchet/zengate) [![Socket](https://badge.socket.dev/npm/package/zengate/latest)](https://socket.dev/npm/package/zengate/overview/latest) [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.scorecard.dev/projects/github.com/developingchet/zengate/badge)](https://scorecard.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/developingchet/zengate) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) An **OpenAI-compatible API for OpenCode's free Zen models: no Zen account or upstream API key needed.** Point any OpenAI SDK or tool at it and use models like `big-pickle`. It supports Chat Completions, the Responses API, streaming, function calling, JSON output and image, audio, video and PDF input. ```mermaid flowchart LR app["Your app
(any OpenAI SDK or tool)"] -->|"OpenAI API + gateway key"| zg["zengate"] zg -->|"loopback, random password"| oc["opencode serve
(private, isolated)"] oc --> zen["OpenCode Zen
free models"] ``` - [How it works](#how-it-works-and-why-it-is-keyless) - [Install](#install) - [Use it from your client](#use-it-from-your-client) - [API compatibility](#api-compatibility) - [Configuration](#configuration) - [Strict conversational profile](#strict-conversational-profile) - [Deployment](#deployment) - [Security](#security) - [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) - [Development](#development) ## How it works (and why it is keyless) OpenCode's free Zen models only work from inside OpenCode. So this gateway does not imitate OpenCode. It **runs the real OpenCode CLI** (`opencode serve`, installed automatically as an npm dependency) as a private backend and translates between the OpenAI API and OpenCode sessions: - Every API request becomes a short-lived OpenCode session, which is deleted afterwards. - The managed backend listens only on `127.0.0.1` with a random password, and its home and config directories are throwaway temp dirs, so your own OpenCode or Claude settings, agents and plugins are never loaded. This configuration isolation is not an operating-system sandbox. - **Managed OpenCode host tools are refused.** The default profile denies execute/browser access and asks then rejects other tool permissions; strict chat removes all host tools and denies every permission. Attached servers require their own equivalent controls (see [Attach mode](#attach-mode)). Attachment downloads requested by API clients are handled separately by the gateway. - Your API key protects *the gateway*. Nothing upstream needs a key. One request, end to end: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant C as Client participant G as zengate participant O as opencode serve (127.0.0.1) participant Z as OpenCode Zen C->>G: POST /v1/chat/completions (Bearer key) G->>G: auth, rate limit, queue slot, parse, build prompt G->>O: create session (tool permissions: ask, execute/browser: deny) G->>O: send prompt O->>Z: model request Z-->>O: tokens O-->>G: events (text, reasoning, permission requests) G->>O: reject every tool permission G-->>C: OpenAI response or SSE chunks G->>O: delete session ``` Trade-offs to know about: - **Prompt overhead.** The default `compatible` profile carries OpenCode's system prompt and tool list (roughly 6–9k input tokens, largely cache hits), and adds about 1–3 s of latency. The opt-in [strict chat profile](#strict-conversational-profile) removes that backend context and host-tool list, but requires separate provider compatibility checks. - **Sampling parameters are ignored.** Settings like `temperature` and `top_p` cannot be forwarded through OpenCode. The gateway accepts them and lists them in an `x-gateway-ignored-params` response header. - **`max_tokens` is approximate.** OpenCode has no output limit either, so the gateway counts about four characters as a token, cuts the answer there, stops the model and reports `finish_reason: "length"`. As in OpenAI's API, `max_completion_tokens` and `max_output_tokens` include reasoning text and `max_tokens` covers only the answer. Usage for a cut answer is estimated, because OpenCode reports none for a stopped turn. - **Upstream terms apply.** Availability, rate limits and the model list are set by OpenCode Zen and can change at any time. Free models may have their own data policies; see the [Zen docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/zen/). > **Fair use.** zengate talks to Zen only through the official OpenCode CLI and never bypasses its limits or free-tier checks. You are responsible for following OpenCode's terms and fair-use expectations. Run it for yourself or your team, not as a public or resold service. ## Install Pick one. All of them need nothing but Node.js 24+ or Docker. **npx (quickest)** ```bash npx zengate ``` **npm (global command)** ```bash npm install -g zengate zengate ``` **Docker** ```bash docker run -d --name zengate -p 127.0.0.1:8083:8083 -v zengate:/data developingchet/zengate docker exec zengate node index.js setup --show # prints the generated key ``` Images are published for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. Each release is tagged with its exact version (for example `1.4.2`) and moves `1.4`, `1` and `latest`; pre-releases get only their exact version tag. The same image is on GitHub Container Registry as `ghcr.io/developingchet/zengate`, and the npm package is on GitHub Packages as `@developingchet/zengate`. Installing from GitHub Packages needs a GitHub token, so npmjs.com and Docker Hub remain the simplest sources. **Docker Compose** ```yaml services: zengate: image: developingchet/zengate:1 restart: unless-stopped ports: - "127.0.0.1:8083:8083" volumes: - zengate:/data # Longer than SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS plus 5s, so in-flight requests can finish. stop_grace_period: 20s cap_drop: [ALL] security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"] # OpenCode writes only to /tmp and the gateway only to /data. read_only: true tmpfs: [/tmp] volumes: zengate: ``` **From source** ```bash git clone https://github.com/developingchet/zengate.git cd zengate npm ci npm start ``` ### First start The gateway creates a config file with a random API key and says where it is. The key itself is not printed, so it does not end up in service logs. Abridged output: ``` Created a gateway API key and saved it to /home/you/.config/zengate/config.json. Use it as the OpenAI API key in your client. To see it, run `zengate setup --show` or read API_KEY from that file; `zengate setup --rotate` replaces it. OpenCode 2.2.6 backend ready (managed, isolated, tools disabled) OpenAI-compatible API on http://127.0.0.1:8083/v1 (auth: API key) 9 models: big-pickle, ... ``` The model count and list come live from OpenCode Zen and change over time. In Docker, run `docker exec zengate node index.js setup --show`; under systemd, read `/var/lib/zengate/config.json` with `sudo`. Where the config file lives: | How you run it | Config file | |---|---| | From source | `config.json` in the project folder | | npm / npx on Linux | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/zengate/config.json` (usually `~/.config/zengate/config.json`) | | npm / npx on macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/zengate/config.json` | | npm / npx on Windows | `%APPDATA%\zengate\config.json` | | Docker | `/data/config.json` (the volume) | Set `CONFIG_FILE` to use any other path. Key commands (`npm run setup -- ` from a source checkout): ```bash zengate setup # create a key if none exists zengate setup --rotate # replace the key zengate setup --show # print the saved key zengate setup --print # print a fresh key without saving it (for env vars and secret stores) zengate --help # also -h or help zengate --version # also -v or version ``` ### Running without a key If only trusted local programs can reach the port, you can turn authentication off explicitly: ```bash ALLOW_NO_AUTH=true zengate ``` The gateway warns at startup when auth is off. Keep `HOST=127.0.0.1` in that case: with auth off, any local process can use the API, and so can any web page if you enable CORS. ## Use it from your client Anything that accepts an OpenAI base URL and API key works: the official SDKs, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Open WebUI, Continue, Aider, LiteLLM and so on. | Setting | Value | |---|---| | Base URL | `http://127.0.0.1:8083/v1` | | API key | the `sk-zg-...` key from first start | | Model | an id from `GET /v1/models`, for example `big-pickle` | ```bash export OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8083/v1 export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-zg-... ``` **Python** ```python from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI() # reads the two variables above r = client.chat.completions.create(model="big-pickle", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]) print(r.choices[0].message.content) ``` **JavaScript / TypeScript** ```js import OpenAI from "openai"; const client = new OpenAI(); // reads the two variables above const stream = await client.responses.create({ model: "big-pickle", input: "Write a haiku about gates.", stream: true }); for await (const event of stream) if (event.type === "response.output_text.delta") process.stdout.write(event.delta); ``` **curl** ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:8083/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"big-pickle","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello!"}]}' ``` ## API compatibility | Endpoint | Status | |---|---| | `POST /v1/chat/completions` | Streaming (SSE, `stream_options.include_usage`), `n` 1–4, `stop`, `tools` / `tool_choice` / `parallel_tool_calls`, legacy `functions`, `response_format` (`json_object`, `json_schema`), `reasoning_effort`, `developer` / `system` / `tool` roles, `reasoning_content` in responses | | `POST /v1/responses` | Streaming with the standard event sequence, `instructions`, `previous_response_id`, `item_reference`, `function` and `custom` tools, `text.format`, `reasoning.effort` / `reasoning` summary items, `store` | | `GET` / `DELETE /v1/responses/{id}` | Stored in memory for 1 hour, within `RESPONSES_STORE_MAX` entries and `RESPONSES_STORE_MB` | | `GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/models/{id}` | Live list from OpenCode | | `GET /health`, `GET /ready` | Public liveness and readiness probes, with no `/v1` prefix (`/ready` answers `503` while starting or shutting down) | | `POST /v1/completions` | Legacy text completions: `prompt` as a string or list of strings, `n`, `stop`, `max_tokens`, `echo`, streaming. The model is asked to continue the text, so it behaves like a chat model, not a base model. Without `max_tokens` the length is not limited (OpenAI defaults to 16) | | `POST /v1/embeddings` | `404 unsupported_endpoint`: Zen serves chat models only | | `GET /metrics` | Request counters, latency and time-to-first-token, slot usage and the OpenCode version (needs the key, no `/v1` prefix). JSON by default; Prometheus text format for `?format=prometheus` or an `Accept: text/plain` scrape | The `/v1` routes also work without the prefix; `/health`, `/ready` and `/metrics` exist only without it. Errors use the standard OpenAI envelope, `{"error": {"message", "type", "param", "code"}}`, with matching HTTP status codes (400, 401, 403, 404, 413, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504). An unknown path returns `404 unknown_url`. Upstream allowance exhaustion returns HTTP 429 with `code: "upstream_quota_exhausted"`; temporary provider throttling uses `upstream_rate_limited`. Validated provider timing appears as `Retry-After` seconds on HTTP errors and `error.retry_after` seconds in the JSON envelope, including Chat/Completions SSE errors and Responses `response.failed` events. Multi-hour delays are preserved. If timing is absent or invalid, both fields are omitted: the reset time is unknown. Structured quota classification needs OpenCode 2.1.2+ (bundled); older backends can report an unclassified 429, which remains `upstream_rate_limited`. The gateway never infers quota classification from human-readable error text. **Inputs** (validated against each model's capabilities; a model that can't take an input returns `400 unsupported_modality`): | Kind | Chat Completions | Responses | |---|---|---| | Text | `text` parts | `input_text` | | Images | `image_url` (data URI or https) | `input_image` | | Audio | `input_audio` (base64 `data` and `format`) | `input_audio` | | Video | `video_url` (data URI or https) | `input_video` | | PDF / files | `file` (`file_data` as a data URI, or bare base64 with a `filename`; or an https `file_url`) | `input_file` (`file_data` / `file_url`) | These media inputs are available in the default `compatible` profile. Strict `chat` accepts text only and rejects media before downloads or model dispatch. In compatibility mode, text files (plain text, markdown, JSON, CSV and so on) are inlined as text, so every model can read them. The gateway downloads `https` attachment URLs itself (at most 16 in one request, 30 seconds each, up to 3 redirects) and passes the content on, so remote files obey `MAX_MEDIA_MB` and `MAX_BODY_MB` like inline ones. The server's `Content-Type` must match the part: an `image_url` must return an image. This direct connection does not use `HTTPS_PROXY`. **Function calling** is emulated. OpenCode sessions cannot register your functions natively, so their schemas go into the prompt and the model's calls come back as standard `tool_calls` or `function_call` items. Results depend on the model and provider. In the default `compatible` profile, if a model tries to call a function the wrong way, or ignores `tool_choice: "required"`, the gateway retries once with a correction. Strict `chat` disables that corrective replay. **Not supported** (clear 400 error): `logprobs`, `suffix`, audio output, `file_id` references (there is no Files API), `background` responses, the Conversations API and stored prompts. Hosted tools such as `web_search` in Responses are ignored and listed in `x-gateway-ignored-params`. ## Configuration Set values as environment variables or in the config file (same names; see [`config.json.example`](config.json.example)). Environment variables win. Invalid values stop startup with a message that names every problem, and so do unknown keys in the config file (`$schema` is allowed). | Setting | Default | Range | Meaning | |---|---|---|---| | `API_KEY` / `API_KEYS` | generated | 16+ chars | Gateway key(s). `API_KEYS` takes a list for rotation. Well-known placeholders such as `change-me` are refused. | | `ALLOW_NO_AUTH` | `false` | | Serve without any key (explicit opt-out). Requests must then use an IP address, `localhost`, a `*.localhost` name or a name in `ALLOWED_HOSTS` as their Host (`403 host_not_allowed` otherwise), which stops web pages from reaching the gateway through DNS rebinding. `/health` and `/ready` are exempt. | | `ALLOWED_HOSTS` | none | list | Extra Host names accepted while `ALLOW_NO_AUTH` is on, such as the name a reverse proxy forwards. | | `HOST` / `PORT` | `127.0.0.1` / `8083` | port 1–65535 | Listen address. | | `MAX_CONCURRENT` / `MAX_QUEUE` | `8` / `32` | 1–64 / 0–1000 | Parallel generations, and how many requests may wait (then `429`). | | `QUEUE_TIMEOUT_MS` | `30000` | 1000–3600000 | How long a request may wait for a slot (then `429`). Keep it below your proxy's response timeout. | | `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` | `120` | 0–100000 | Per client IP; IPv6 clients count per /64 network. `0` turns it off. | | `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` | `300000` | 10000–3600000 | Per generation, counted from when it gets a slot (then `504`). | | `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS` | `10000` | 1000–3600000 | How long a shutdown waits for in-flight requests. Give Docker or systemd at least 5 seconds more. | | `MAX_BODY_MB` / `MAX_MEDIA_MB` | `25` / `20` | 1–200 / 1–100 | R …[文件过长——仅保留首 16KB 与末 8KB]… `--stop-timeout 20` (or `stop_grace_period` in Compose) to let in-flight requests finish. The image runs as the unprivileged `node` user and works with a read-only root (`--read-only --tmpfs /tmp`), `--cap-drop ALL` and `--security-opt no-new-privileges:true`, as in the Compose example above. On shutdown, `/ready` answers `503` for up to 2 seconds before the listener closes, so a load balancer polling it stops sending traffic first. **systemd.** See [`deploy/zengate.service`](deploy/zengate.service). It runs as an unprivileged user with a hardened sandbox and a system-call filter (`@system-service`), and the key goes in `/var/lib/zengate/config.json`. **Behind a reverse proxy.** Set `TRUST_PROXY=1` (or however many hops you have) so rate limits apply per real client. Disable response buffering for streaming. The gateway already sends `X-Accel-Buffering: no` for nginx. ### Verifying releases Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign) (keyless, from this repository's release workflow) and carry a CycloneDX SBOM attestation. Current releases are signed with cosign 3, whose signature and bundle format cosign 2 cannot read, so verify with cosign 3 or later: ```bash cosign verify developingchet/zengate:1 \ --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github.com/developingchet/zengate/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v' \ --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com ``` npm releases are published from GitHub Actions with [provenance](https://docs.npmjs.com/generating-provenance-statements); `npm audit signatures` checks it. Each GitHub release also lists SHA-256 checksums. From 1.0.4, `checksums.txt` and the package tarball are signed with cosign too: ```bash cosign verify-blob checksums.txt --bundle checksums.txt.sigstore.json \ --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github.com/developingchet/zengate/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v' \ --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com sha256sum -c checksums.txt ``` ## Security - The API key is required unless you set `ALLOW_NO_AUTH`. Keys are compared in constant time, the config file is written with mode `0600`, and keys are never logged: the first start reports where the generated key was saved, not the key. - The gateway binds to loopback by default and warns when it listens elsewhere, because traffic is plain HTTP, so put TLS in front. - The managed backend isolates OpenCode from your home directory and configuration and rejects host tools. Attached servers need equivalent operator-managed permissions; see [Attach mode](#attach-mode). - Attachment URLs must be `https` and resolve to public addresses. Loopback, private, link-local and similar ranges (including IPv6 forms that embed them) are refused, which blocks SSRF into your network. The gateway fetches them itself and connects only to the address it checked, including on every redirect, so DNS rebinding cannot reach an internal host. OpenCode never sees the URL. - Conversation history is sent to the model as a tagged transcript. Message text, file names and tool names are escaped so they cannot fake another turn, a tool result or a function call. - Rate limiting, a bounded queue with a wait limit, body and attachment size limits, and per-request timeouts all apply. Requests that are uploading, queued or running are capped at `MAX_CONCURRENT + MAX_QUEUE`, which bounds the memory held by request bodies, and one client address may be uploading at most a quarter of that at once. Attachment hosts are resolved inside the request's slot and timeout, with at most two DNS lookups in flight across the gateway. Attachment URLs appear in errors and logs as their origin only, without path, query string or credentials. A request with `n` choices uses `n` concurrency slots, and slots are always released on disconnect or timeout. - Stored responses (`previous_response_id`, `GET /v1/responses/{id}`) are visible only to the API key that created them. - The gateway sends no telemetry and never logs request bodies. OpenCode's auto-update and session sharing are disabled. To report a vulnerability, see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Fix | |---|---| | `401 invalid_api_key` | Send `Authorization: Bearer `. | | `403 host_not_allowed` | Auth is off and the request's Host is not an IP address or `localhost`. Add the name to `ALLOWED_HOSTS`. | | `404 model_not_found` | Use an id from `GET /v1/models`. The free model list changes over time. | | `404 unknown_url` | Check the path. `/health`, `/ready` and `/metrics` have no `/v1` prefix. | | `413 request_too_large` | The body exceeds `MAX_BODY_MB`. | | `400 unsupported_modality` | The model cannot take this input kind, or strict chat rejected media. Strict chat accepts text only. | | `400 attachment_too_large` | An attachment exceeds `MAX_MEDIA_MB`. | | `400 invalid_attachment_url` | The attachment URL is not public, failed to download, or returned the wrong type. Send it as a base64 data URI instead. | | `400 previous_response_not_found` | The stored response expired (1 hour), was evicted, was created with another key or with `store: false`, or storage is off. | | `400 context_length_exceeded` | The conversation is too long for the model. Trim history or pick a model with a larger context. | | `400 upstream_rejected` / `backend_rejected` | The model provider or OpenCode refused the request as sent; the message gives the reason. | | `429 server_busy` / `rate_limit_exceeded` | Raise `MAX_CONCURRENT` / `MAX_QUEUE` / `QUEUE_TIMEOUT_MS` / `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`, or slow down. | | `429 upstream_quota_exhausted` | Provider allowance is exhausted. Wait for the supplied reset delay; if absent, timing is unknown. The gateway does not bypass quotas. | | `429 upstream_rate_limited`, `502 upstream_*` | OpenCode Zen is throttling or failing. Honor `Retry-After` when present. | | `502 structured_output_failed` | The model did not return JSON matching `response_format` / `text.format`. Retry, simplify the schema, or try another model. | | `503 backend_agent_unavailable` / `backend_chat_profile_unavailable` | Verify the agent/profile settings and the required OpenCode version. The gateway stops before prompt dispatch. | | `503 backend_unavailable` | OpenCode is still starting or restarting. Check `GET /ready`. Run with `LOG_LEVEL=debug` to see OpenCode's own logs. | | Startup: `Port ... in use` | Another process has the port. Set `PORT`. | | Startup: `EACCES` / permission denied binding a port | Check Windows excluded TCP ranges (`netsh interface ipv4 show excludedportrange protocol=tcp`) and select an available `PORT`. | | Startup: `could not be written` | The config folder is read-only. Set `API_KEY`, or point `CONFIG_FILE` somewhere writable. | ## Development ```bash npm test # unit, integration and property-based tests (fake OpenCode server) npm run test:coverage npm run lint # syntax, file size and hygiene checks npm run audit # npm audit of production dependencies npm run test:backend-contract # real bundled CLI, synthetic local provider npm run test:leak # real model tries every tool; fails if anything ran MODEL=big-pickle npm run test:chat-live # strict chat against a real model GATEWAY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8083/v1 API_KEY=sk-zg-... npm run test:live # a running gateway, real models ``` Code map: - `index.js` and `src/cli.js`: the `zengate` command; `src/config.js`: settings and validation. - `src/opencode/`: backend supervisor, isolation, HTTP client, event hub, session runner, model catalog and the strict-chat plugin. - `src/openai/`: request parsing, prompt building, media and attachment downloads, streaming, and the Chat, Responses and Completions handlers. - `src/server/`: Express app, auth, CORS, limits and errors. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how to propose changes and cut releases, and [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for release notes. ## License MIT. zengate is an independent project, not affiliated with OpenCode or OpenAI.
